title: heavyweight-uwf-arena-1998
label: Mighty Quinn

won.source: Won the vacant championship in the promotion's own Heavyweight Royal Rumble broadcast, eliminating Snake Zurlock last.

note: Still champion at this record's own latest 2000 data point, a 13 May 2000 ranking update.

title: heavyweight-uwf-arena-1998
label: Pure Pain

won.source: Billed as the reigning UWF Heavyweight Champion on the promotion's own "Rage for Order" card, 8 January 1999.

note: Lost the title to Holy Terror in a match not read for this record, some time between 22 January and 3 February 1999.

title: arena-uwf-arena-1998
label: Powerhouse

won.source: Billed as the reigning, undefeated UWF Arena Champion in the promotion's own 1998 year-end awards and 8 January 1999 all-time rankings.

note: Survived a non-title loss to Biohazard on "Rage for Order" without relinquishing the title.

won.source: Billed as the reigning UWF Tag Team Champions in the promotion's own 8 January 1999 all-time rankings.

title: superheavyweight-uwf-arena-1998
label: Hyena Cornwall

won.source: Billed as the reigning UWF Superheavyweight Champion in the promotion's own 8 January 1999 all-time rankings.

note: Lost the title to ToNiK in a match not read for this record, between 9 January and 22 January 1999.

title: superheavyweight-uwf-arena-1998
label: ToNiK

won.source: Billed as the reigning UWF Superheavyweight Champion in the promotion's own 22 January 1999 Cold War II roster.

note: The promotion vacated the title on 11 February 1999 after severing ties with ToNiK's own handler over his conduct toward the promotion's president; a Battle for the Belt tournament was announced to crown a new champion.

title: lightweight-uwf-arena-1998
label: Mack

won.source: Billed as the new UWF Lightweight Champion in the promotion's own 13 May 2000 ranking update, having interfered against the previous champion, Diabolus, at Blackout the month before.

note: Still champion at this record's own latest 2000 data point.

title: gangwarfare-uwf-arena-1998
label: Buzzard

won.source: Billed as the reigning UWF Gang Warfare Champion in the promotion's own 8 January 1999 all-time rankings.

note: The promotion's own 22 January 1999 Cold War II roster separately tags both Mr. Grunge and Top Dawg's stable as Gang Warfare Champions; the discrepancy is not resolved in the documents read for this record.

title: heavyweight-uwf-arena-1998
label: Holy Terror

won.source: Billed by the promotion's own 3 February 1999 broadcast as the recent dethroner of the UWF Heavyweight Championship.

note: Lost a non-title match to a debuting Johnny Reb on "Blackout," after which the promotion's own broadcast declared the championship and its own top ten rankings in "utter turmoil," pending resolution.

title: heavyweight-uwf-arena-1998
label: JJ Rock

won.source: This title change is not shown in the surviving record; the promotion's own last attested 1999 champion is Holy Terror, and JJ Rock is later named as the title's abandoning holder in the 2000 Heavyweight Royal Rumble broadcast.

how: Abandoned the title rather than defend it, described in the promotion's own words as having "won the UWF Championship and left it to rot," leaving it vacant ahead of the Heavyweight Royal Rumble.
note: This gap in the ledger, between Holy Terror's last 1999 attestation and JJ Rock's own abandonment, falls on the promotion's own weekly broadcasts not held in this record.

won.source: Billed as the reigning UWF Lightweight Champion in the promotion's own 8 January 1999 all-time rankings and 11 February 1999 stable report.

title: lightweight-uwf-arena-1998
label: Diabolus

won.source: This title change is not shown in the surviving record; the promotion's own last attested 1999 champion is The Scissor. Diabolus is billed the reigning champion by April 2000, retaining the title against John E. Holmes at Blackout.

how: The title change itself is not shown in the surviving record; the promotion's own 2 May 2000 ranking still bills him champion, and its 13 May 2000 ranking bills Mack as champion instead.
note: Two undocumented gaps bracket this reign: how Diabolus took the title from The Scissor, and how Mack took it from Diabolus, both on weekly broadcasts not held in this record.
